chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the meat of horses, and he said: Do not eat it unless necessity befalls you. [And about] the meat of domestic donkeys. He said in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) that he forbids eating it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating horse and donkey meat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the distinct rulings for horse and domestic donkey meat, noting that while horse meat is generally disliked (makruh) but permissible during necessity, the meat of domestic donkeys is prohibited based on the view attributed to Imam Ali in his book. The narration highlights the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between wild and domestic donkeys, with the latter being strictly forbidden, reflecting the broader Islamic legal principle of preserving dignity and health in dietary laws.
